page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Open system
lines: Open system: exchanges both matter and
Example: water heated in an open beaker —
steps.why: The three system types are separated by one test: what crosses the boundary. In an open system both matter and energy cross.
common_mistakes: Giving an example without naming what crosses — say which part is the matter and which is the energy.
steps.memory_tip: Open beaker: steam out, heat in — both kinds of exchange in one picture.
steps.margin_note: Definition plus one example with both exchanges named.

steps.label: Closed system
lines: Closed system: exchanges energy but not
Example: water heated in a sealed copper
vessel — heat passes through the walls,

lines.text: Open: matter and energy cross. Closed: only energy.

steps.why: Sealing the vessel stops matter, but conducting walls still pass heat — that one difference is what makes the system closed rather than open or isolated.
common_mistakes: Confusing closed with isolated — an isolated system blocks energy as well, a closed system does not.
steps.memory_tip: Sealed but conducting walls: matter is stopped, energy still passes.
steps.margin_note: The boundary material decides: sealed but conducting = closed.

insider_note: One mark per system, and each example only completes its mark if it names what actually crosses the boundary. Keep closed apart from isolated: a closed system still lets energy through.
